etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Medieval Latin intimidatus, past participle of intimidō (“to make afraid”), from Latin in- (“in”) + timidus (“afraid, timid”); see timid.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make timid or afraid; to cause to feel fear or nervousness; to deter, especially by threats of violence.

quote.citation: 2018, Nnedi Okorafor, Who Fears Death, HarperVoyager, page 168:
quote.text: His father tried to intimidate his son into staying, threatening him with banishment and a possible beating.
